naslov: How to Protect Our Children in These Difficult Times

segmenti.tekst: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ نَحْمَدُهُ وَنَسْتَعِينُهُ وَنَسْتَغْفِرُهُ
segmenti.prevod: All praise belongs to Allah; we praise Him, seek His help and ask His forgiveness.

segmenti.tekst: وَنَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شُرُورِ أَنْفُسِنَا وَمِنْ سَيِّئَاتِ أَعْمَالِنَا مَنْ يَهْدِهِ اللَّهُ فَلَا مُضِلَّ لَهُ، وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهُ
segmenti.prevod: We seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls and from our bad deeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can lead astray, and whomever He leaves astray, none can guide.

segmenti.tekst: وَأَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ
segmenti.prevod: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, Who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger.

segmenti.tekst: أَرْسَلَهُ اللَّهُ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا وَسِرَاجًا مُنِيرًا لِيُنْذِرَ مَنْ كَانَ حَيًّا وَيَحِقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ الطَّيِّبِينَ الطَّاهِرِينَ وَأَصْحَابِهِ الْكِرَامِ الْهُدَاةِ الْمُهْتَدِينَ وَسَلَّمَ تَسْلِيمًا كَثِيرًا إِلَى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ
segmenti.prevod: Allah sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings, a warner and a light-giving lamp, to warn whoever is alive (of heart) and so that the Word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers (Ya-Sin 36:70). May Allah the Exalted bless him and his good and pure family and his noble companions, the rightly guided who guided others, and grant him abundant peace until the Day of Judgement.

segmenti.tekst: قَالَ اللَّهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ الْكَرِيمِ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ أَمَّا بَعْدُ
segmenti.prevod: Allah says in His noble Book: “O you who believe, fear Allah as He deserves to be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.” (Al Imran 3:102). To proceed:

segmenti.tekst: …of the worlds, Lord of the Day of Judgment, Lord of jinn and mankind. May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.

Dear brothers, respected congregation, our children are our responsibility and our obligation. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala (glorified and exalted is He), commands us in the Qur'an to raise our children, to take care of our children, with the words: “O believers, protect yourselves and your families

from the Fire of Jahannam (Hellfire), whose fuel will be people and stones.” This verse is the basis and a clear command from Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, that we should take care of our children while they grow up, and afterwards as well, and raise them in a good way. And for a person to raise his child in a good and correct way, several things are needed.

The first thing is that a person makes dua (supplication) for his child, that he turns to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Informing us about the servants of the Most Merciful, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in the Qur'an: “My Lord, make our spouses and our children a comfort to our eyes.”

That they be our joy, and not our sorrow. So a person should supplicate for his child, ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, for his child. We also have the supplication of Ibrahim, alayhis-salatu was-salam, where Ibrahim, alayhis-salatu was-salam, says: “Rabbij'alni muqima as-salati wa min dhurriyyati, Rabbana wa taqabbal du'a'” – my Lord, make me and my descendants among those who establish the prayer, who are steadfast in prayer. The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, also says:

“The supplication of three is not rejected,” among them the supplication of a parent. The supplication of a parent [unclear] for his child is not rejected. So when a parent asks Allah for something for his child, Allah will not turn that supplication back. That is why it is very important for a person to pray for his child, and not against his child. And we will see, unfortunately, that many parents curse their children while they are small, because of some small mischief they did, and then the child, when he grows up –

Allah accepts that supplication, and then the child is disobedient, bad, and so on. I don't know where those parents' sense is in such situations. Say: “May Allah guide you, may Allah grant you long life, may Allah set you right,” and not something else. The second thing is that the parent be a role model for his child, that he be a good example for his child.
First in obedience to Allah, and after that that he be honest, good, a good believer. And then the child – what does the child do? The child imitates, follows his parent, follows his parent.

A person cannot tell his child: “Here's 300 dinars for a snack, but don't go to the betting shop,” while he himself goes to the betting shop, he himself bets. A person cannot smoke cigarettes and tell his child: “Don't let me catch you lighting up.” Or a person drinks alcohol, goes to the tavern every night, and tells his child: “Don't let me see you,” he says, “drinking alcohol.” What kind of example is that? That is not an example, that is not a role model.

Rather, a role model – that a person be honest, good, and then the child, when he sees that his father is good and honest, will follow him in that. Also, the mother should be an example to her daughter: in dress, in behavior, at home, outside the home.

Because if the daughter sees that her mother talks back to her father, of course, tomorrow when she grows up, she will do the same. That is why it is very important for a person to be an example to his child, because we are the mirror of our children.
The third thing is that a person makes an effort, that he does not give up in raising his children. That he does not raise his child today and abandon him to the street tomorrow.
Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in the Qur'an, commanding our Prophet, with the words: “And command your family to perform the prayer,” and what? “Be steadfast in it.”
There is no giving up. Rather, every day a person, a person should follow, watch how his child behaves, whether he is behaving properly, and so on.

The fourth thing is providing the means that benefit the child, that benefit the upbringing of the child itself. That a person takes his child and brings him to the mekteb (Qur'an school), so that he learns the basics of the religion, the basics of good manners, so that he knows who his Lord is, who his Prophet is, so that he knows how to behave toward his parents, toward his neighbors; that he takes his child along to a lecture; that he takes his child and brings him to Jumu'ah, and sits him down next to himself.

These are the means. It doesn't have to be only a lecture – some useful things, dear brothers: let him take him to educational classes, on how to protect the environment, history classes, geography, everything that is beneficial, that is good. Also, that he keep him away from the means that destroy a child's upbringing,
such as today's phones, such as today's websites that promote immoral things, immoral acts; that he limit the child's phone and the playing of games that promote violence.

We have seen, dear brothers, what happened in Turkey these days. That a game that was played, called PUBG, so destroyed the minds of those children. Games that promote violence, where we have online chat, voice chat, where we have swearing and giving orders, and so on, and so forth.

And then what do we have? We have a monster child, who will take a pistol and go and kill several of his peers, not… dozens, and then in the end simply commit suicide. A person should follow these trends, follow these things, and not leave his child to these things.
The sixth thing, dear brothers, is that a person, a believer, a mu'min, directs his child to good company. To company that is good. That he not let him spend time with ill-mannered children.
The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: …so let a person look carefully at whom he befriends. As our people would say: you are who you keep company with.
Has a healthy apple ever made the rotten ones become healthy? Never. One rotten apple spoils hundreds of healthy apples.
That is why, dear brothers, we should direct our children to good company, but not only our children, but ourselves as well. Ourselves as well. The seventh thing is that a person be aware

that raising children is a religious obligation. Just as it is your obligation to perform the prayer, the five daily prayers, just as it is your obligation to give zakah, just as it is your obligation to be kind to your parents, it is your obligation to raise your children and direct them to the right path, because otherwise you will be a great sinner, just as the one who abandons the prayer is a great sinner – although there is a dilemma there, whether he is a sinner or a disbeliever, there is great disagreement among the scholars –

or the one who abandons zakah, the giving of zakah, out of negligence, or the one who is disobedient to his parents – that is a major sin. And whoever abandons the upbringing of his children, let him know that he is a great, great sinner.

The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: “Kullukum ra'in” – each of you is a shepherd, the master in his own house – “and each of you is,” what? “Responsible for his flock,” for his household. Each of us, the head of the household, is responsible for his family, for his children, for his wife.

Also, among the things that help a person to guide his child correctly, to bring him up, is that a person reads, studies the biographies of good people, of Allah's servants, and sees how they brought up their children, in what way.

And the most beautiful example for us is the Qur'anic example of the good man Luqman. Let a person take Surah Luqman and read it: in the first place he commands him to worship Allah alone, subhanahu wa ta'ala, not to commit shirk with Him.

In the second, to be obedient to his parents, that is, to be one who is kind to his parents, not to walk arrogantly on the earth, that injustice is a great sin, and so on. That he become acquainted with these biographies.

Also, dear brothers, it is that a person not be in a hurry for results. If the child does not obey today, he will obey tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, after that, and so on, and so forth. A person must by no means make a mistake in the upbringing of his children, so that the child later runs away from both father and mother and everything.

Rather, sabr (patience) is needed, and that a person not hurry, because haste is from Satan. Haste is from Satan. And the last thing, and perhaps the most important of all these things, is that a person watches over his child's prayer.

But first he must watch over his own prayer, in order to watch over his child's prayer. Because it is the connection between the servant and the Lord, it is the connection between Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, and His servants. When that connection is cut, everything is lost, everything else is irrelevant. A person can then be this and that, but if he cuts the connection with Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, then these nine things we have listed are of no use to him. None. And a little earlier we cited the verse in which Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, commands the Prophet with the words:

“Wa'mur ahlaka bis-salati wastabir 'alayha” – and command your family to perform the prayer and be steadfast in it. Informing us about Isma'il, alayhis-salatu was-salam, [unclear], what does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say? He says: he used to command his family to perform the prayer.

The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: “Command your children to perform the prayer from the age of seven, and give them a light smack if they do not pray when they reach ten years.” How important the prayer is! “And separate them in their beds.”

These, dear brothers, are pieces of advice worth gold, especially in today's times. Times that are alarming, wallahi, alarming. Whoever has children who go to school, and children who tell him what goes on in the schools and how children behave in the schools – wallahi, our situation is alarming.

And let us not be surprised that we have such a situation on the streets, with the traffic, that we have such a situation in the city, that our streets are dirty, that what is happening to us is happening.

All of it, all of it is negligence in raising children, because a child learns when he is small. A person cannot be brought up when he turns 20, that is finished; rather, a child learns while he is small. A person cannot, as we said a little earlier, smoke cigarettes and forbid that to his child; go to the betting shop and forbid that to his child; fill up a whole bag of garbage, open the window and throw it into the middle of the street, and at the same time tell his child: “Don't do that, don't throw this garbage,” and so on.

He himself must be a decent person, be an example, especially we here in the mosque, who come to the mosque, who listen to all of this – we have the greatest responsibility, the greatest responsibility. That is why, dear brothers, let us protect our families from the Fire of Jahannam, let us protect our children, let us follow them and bring them up in the right, correct way, the way with which Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will be pleased with both them and us.

May He make our children the comfort of our eyes, may He help our brothers in Gaza, may He help the Muslims in every place where a battle is fought so that the word of Allah and His pleasure be uppermost and the word of disbelief be lowest, may He protect us from every evil, and forgive the sins of our parents.
آمِينَ يَا رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ
segmenti.prevod: Amen, O Lord of the worlds.

segmenti.tekst: أَقُولُ قَوْلِي هَٰذَا وَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ لِي وَلَكُمْ فَاسْتَغْفِرُوهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
segmenti.prevod: I say these words of mine and ask Allah for forgiveness for myself and for you, so ask Him for forgiveness; truly He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
